ig_carousel_topic.topic: Bankroll math for people who've never thought about bankroll
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Most bettors lose money before they place a single bad pick.
The reason is bankroll management, or the lack of it.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common approach: bet whatever feels right.
$50 on one game. $200 on the next because it 'feels stronger.'
That's not a strategy. That's variance with a wallet.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Flat betting fixes this.
Pick a unit size, typically 1% to 2% of your total bankroll, and bet that amount on every single play.
A $500 bankroll means $5 to $10 per bet. Every bet.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Say your bankroll is $500 and your unit is $10 (2%).
At a 54% win rate over 100 bets, flat betting at -110 juice nets roughly +8 to +12 units, or $80 to $120.
Sizing up randomly on 'strong' picks erases that edge fast.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
A 54% win rate is genuinely profitable. Most people never see those profits because their sizing is chaotic.
Consistent unit sizing is the only thing that turns a real edge into real money over time.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Bankroll math isn't complicated. Most bettors just skip it. This is the part that actually determines whether a winning record makes money.
